logline: Two teenagers dig their way to the surface from an underground village, commandeer a drill-powered mecha, and ignite a rebellion that escalates from overthrowing a tyrant king to saving all of existence.

renewal.note: The 27-episode series concluded in September 2007. Two compilation films - Gurren-hen (2008) and Lagann-hen (2009) - followed. Studio Trigger, founded by Gurren Lagann director Hiroyuki Imaishi, now holds rights as of 2021.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 17 critics and 90% audience score; IMDb 8.3 from a large voter base; critics consensus cites 'brilliant animation, charismatic characters, and subversive writing'.

pull_quotes.text: This subterranean romp blazes on the screen with brilliant animation, charismatic characters, and subversive writing.

seasons.review_body: Gainax aired Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann on TV Tokyo from April to September 2007, and it arrived as one of the studio's most accessible and critically embraced works. The series earned 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 17 critics - a perfect score that held across more than a decade of catalogue additions - and an IMDb audience score of 8.3. The RT critics consensus credits 'brilliant animation, charismatic characters, and subversive writing.' Directed by Hiroyuki Imaishi, whose kinetic style later defined Studio Trigger, the series operates in two distinct acts: a boisterous surface-war in the first half and a cosmic-scale confrontation in the second, with critics noting the shift could have killed the momentum but instead delivered its biggest emotional payoffs. The death of fan-favourite Kamina at the midpoint is consistently cited by reviewers as one of anime's most effective structural gambles.

episode_reviews.title: Farewell, Comrades
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode that reshaped the entire series. Kamina's arc ends here, and the show makes a structural bet that losing its most charismatic character will deepen rather than deflate the rest of the run. Critics and fans uniformly call it the pivotal hour of the series.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Simon cradles Kamina in the cockpit. The 'Who the hell do you think I am?' speech is delivered, and its weight only increases in every episode that follows.

episode_reviews.title: The Sky Is Yours
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale delivers the cosmic payoff promised since the series' tone expanded in episode 17. Critics praised it for earning its scale through character work rather than spectacle alone - Simon's arc closes cleanly, and the epilogue lands with unusual emotional grace for a mecha series.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Simon drives the drill into the Anti-Spiral. Everything the series told you about believing in yourself is crystallised in a single image.
